author: ValWood
body:
I think it is indirect:

GDP-mannose is a central sugar-nucleotide donor in yeast  serving as the activated form of mannose used for essentially all mannosylation reactions in the cell. Its main roles are:

1. Protein glycosylation (its biggest job)

Yeast cell walls and secreted proteins are heavily mannosylated, and GDP-mannose supplies the mannose for both major pathways:

N-linked glycosylation: In the cytosol/ER, GDP-mannose donates mannose directly to the growing dolichol-linked oligosaccharide precursor (the early Man₅GlcNAc₂ steps) and is also used to make dolichol-phosphate-mannose (Dol-P-Man), which supplies mannose for the later, lumenal steps. In the Golgi, GDP-mannose is imported by the transporter Vrg4 and used by mannosyltransferases (Och1, the mannan polymerase complexes M-Pol I/II, Mnn1 family, etc.) to build the large "outer chain" mannan structures characteristic of yeast glycoproteins.
O-linked mannosylation: Via Dol-P-Man, the PMT family of protein O-mannosyltransferases attaches mannose to serine/threonine residues in the ER, and Golgi enzymes extend these chains using GDP-mannose directly.

2. GPI anchor biosynthesis

The glycan core of glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchors contains three to four mannose residues, all donated (via Dol-P-Man) from GDP-mannose. GPI anchoring is essential in yeast, tethering many proteins to the membrane and cell wall.

3. Cell wall synthesis and integrity

Mannoproteins make up roughly 30–50% of the yeast cell wall mass. Because their mannan chains all trace back to GDP-mannose, it's indispensable for cell wall architecture, porosity, and stress resistance. Mutants with reduced GDP-mannose synthesis or transport (e.g., psa1/vig9 or vrg4 mutants) show severe cell wall defects, osmotic sensitivity, and can be inviable.

--

Note that when we had the same discussion about mannose donors for GPI biosynthesis, the decision was that this was upstream.

Although in some of these cases the boundaries have subsequently changed so I'm not sure......I could be persuaded either way but we need to make a decsion so that we can be consistent
